output.name: Haskeri
output.myth: When Aun cut the string the sky rose so fast that Tavo came down to see the noise. He laughed, and the wind tore through the gull-roost on the cliffs. One gull, grey as wet slate, was thrown too low over the Leeward. It had the names of the drowned in its beak, as gulls do, so that families could hear them said. Tavo spread its wings and would not let them fold. It went south past Halesk, the Stilled Gull, who hangs in the Unflown with her neck up like a hand asking for rain, too proud to come down. It did not stop for her. To the west, the Count of Oars, Tormesk, watched it go. Hesk keeps count of the names; they are still being carried. Look south on a clear night, low over the water, for two faint stars at the wingtips. When they shine, news is coming from the drowned. When they dim, someone should go and ask Kael, the Netter, who has cast for fallen stars all his life and never caught one.
output.finding: Start at Varuk, the Kite Aun Did Not Fly, and go a little less than one hand-span to the south-east, low over the water, until you reach the two faint stars at the gull's wingtips.
